description: Shared Docker IMAGE OS-package inventory contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server (server issue #101). Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/docker_image_inventory_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_docker_image_inventory.py::test_contract_fixture_scenarios (only the Docker SDK boundary -- client.containers.get / container.get_archive -- is mocked). For each scenario, 'sdk' describes the container's filesystem as the agent-side test builds it (files by path, symlinks with their linkTarget, paths that 404 via 'not_found', a DB that overflows the 5 MB cap via 'oversized'); the server ignores 'sdk'. 'payload' is the EXACT body the agent POSTs to /image_packages -- the artifact the server's image-package ingester must parse; copy this file byte-identical into the server spec/fixtures and bump FEATURES_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS['docker_image_inventory'] to agent_min_version exactly. Change only in lockstep. Contract highlights: (a) packages carry {name, version, ecosystem} where ecosystem is null == 'the image OS ecosystem' (a future phase sends npm/pypi/etc. on the same endpoint, no v2); (b) packages_hash reuses the host packages path's get_packages_hash and is null on a failure payload; (c) an extraction failure is NEVER empty-and-clean -- every failure records a structured errors[] entry so the server renders 'not scannable, <reason>' instead of a false '0 vulnerabilities'; (d) the /etc/os-release symlink MUST be followed via stat['linkTarget'] or every Debian image looks unscannable; (e) the dpkg Status filter keeps only 'install ok installed'; (f) RPM is unsupported in phase 1 (reported, not empty).
_agent_min_version_note: Docker image inventory ships in 1.14.0 (the first MINOR after the 1.13.x line: 1.13.0 Ceph v2, 1.13.1 PHP-FPM). The server's FEATURES_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS['docker_image_inventory'] must match this exactly.

config._note: How the server TURNS THIS ON. Without this the server can ship the whole ingester and the agent will never POST anything.
config._image_inventory_note: TOP-LEVEL /collect config key, truthy-checked. It must NOT be nested under config['docker']: collectors.py splats config['docker'] as **kwargs into docker_metrics(), so a new nested key would raise TypeError on every agent older than 1.14.0, get swallowed into data['docker']=null, and (with the never-prune-on-null rule) freeze container-state rows fleet-wide. Agent 1.14.0 also adds **_kwargs to docker_metrics as a belt-and-braces guard, but the key stays top-level regardless.
config._requires_docker: config['docker'] must ALSO be enabled. The agent derives the set of image digests to scan from the already-collected data['docker']['containers'] payload (no second daemon call), so with Docker collection off there are no digests to inventory.
config._join_key: payload['image_id'] == data['docker']['containers'][*]['image_id'] (both are the container's attrs.Image local digest). That join is how the server turns image vulnerabilities into per-container findings.
config._socket_url: config['docker']['socket_url'], when set, is reused verbatim for the archive API connection and is also what the agent's docker capability probe checks.

response_contract._note: The agent's retry/stop behaviour depends on the RESPONSE, and a server that gets this wrong creates a permanent re-extraction treadmill (each retry re-runs archive GETs + tar parse + POST).
response_contract.success_requires_non_empty_json_body: CRITICAL: the agent treats a request as successful when _post returns a TRUTHY parsed JSON body -- not merely on status 200. A 200 with an empty body makes json.loads('') raise (treated as transient, full retry budget burned), and a 200 with '{}' parses to a FALSY dict (also treated as transient). Always return a non-empty JSON object, e.g. {"status":"ok","accepted":true} or {"status":"ok","accepted":false,"reason":"unsupported_distro"}.
response_contract.refusals_are_200: Answer 200 for EVERY definitive outcome, including refusals, so the agent marks the digest done and stops re-extracting an immutable image. Do NOT use 4xx for a permanent refusal (unentitled tenant, unknown image): the agent treats every non-200 as transient and there is no per-digest backoff or circuit breaker.
response_contract.durability: A 200 is a ONE-SHOT commitment: the agent appends the digest to its on-disk done set and never re-sends it (digests are immutable). Persist the payload durably BEFORE responding 200. If ingest is async, a lost write is permanent -- there is no reconciliation path and no server-side way to ask the agent to re-scan a digest.
response_contract.non_200_is_transient: Any non-200 (or a connection failure) releases the digest so it retries on a later tick.

errors_contract._note: errors[] is a CLOSED set the server can switch on. Every value the agent can emit is enumerated here -- do not infer the set from the scenarios below, which exercise only the common ones. (Inferring a value set from an incomplete sample is exactly how the Ceph v2 ingester shipped dead gauges.)

type.not_found: A 404 from the archive API. On the os_release step this is the distroless/scratch signal; on a DB step it means the image has no such package DB. Also how a container removed mid-extraction surfaces -- indistinguishable at the API. Render: not scannable.
type.api_error: Any non-404 daemon/SDK/stream failure. Render: not scannable this time (transient-ish); the digest is still marked done on a 200, so it will not be retried automatically.
type.file_over_cap: The file exceeded the 5 MB per-file cap and was abandoned mid-stream. Render: not scannable.
type.parse_error: The file was read but yielded nothing usable (unreadable tar, unresolved symlink chain, or a DB whose every entry was filtered out). Render: not scannable -- NEVER as '0 vulnerabilities'.
type.unsupported_distro: Either os-release has no ID, or the distro family is out of scope for phase 1 (RPM is phase 1.5). Render: not scannable, unsupported distro.
type.package_cap: HIGHEST-STAKES VALUE. The package list was TRUNCATED to the 2000-package cap. `packages` is a PREFIX, not the whole image. The server MUST NOT treat such a scan as complete -- doing so silently under-reports vulnerabilities, which is the false all-clear this whole error contract exists to prevent. Note this type has no scenario below (a 2001-package fixture would bloat the shared file); it is covered by agent unit tests and pinned by a drift test asserting this enum matches the code.

step.distro: Classifying the parsed distro into a package-DB family.

errors_contract.message_determinism: errors[].message is deterministic -- it never embeds raw SDK exception text, which varies by daemon version. The raw exception goes to the agent's debug log instead. Safe for the server to key on.

packages_contract.ordering: packages is sorted by name, and packages_hash is ORDER-SENSITIVE (it is the concatenation of 'name=version\n' over the list as given). Preserve order if you re-serialize, or the hash will not match.
packages_contract.packages_hash: sha256 over 'name=version\n' per entry, byte-compatible with the host /packages path (same get_packages_hash function). It covers name+version ONLY -- it deliberately does NOT include `ecosystem`. Once a later phase populates ecosystem, two sets differing only in ecosystem would hash identically, so do not use packages_hash as a set identity beyond OS packages. null on a failure payload.
packages_contract.ecosystem_null: null means 'the image's OS ecosystem'. The slot exists so a future phase can send {"name":"lodash","version":"4.17.20","ecosystem":"npm"} on the SAME endpoint without a contract break.
packages_contract.merge_semantics: UNRESOLVED - decide before the language-ecosystem phase. If a POST replaces all packages for an image_id, the future npm POST would wipe the OS packages, and the agent will never re-send them (mark_done is once-per-digest-forever). Upserting by (name, version, ecosystem) avoids that.
packages_contract.field_hygiene: name and version have C0/C1 control characters and U+FFFD stripped and are truncated to 256 chars by the agent; an entry whose name or version scrubs to empty is dropped rather than shipped.

error_path_audit.daemon_unreachable: get_docker_client returns None -> build_image_inventory returns None (NOT a payload) -> the uploader calls on_failure -> the digest is released and retried on a later tick. A transient infra condition is never a scan verdict.
error_path_audit.container_gone_before_extraction: client.containers.get raising NotFound -> build_image_inventory returns None -> retry. A later tick re-picks the digest with whatever container then runs it; if none does, the digest is never learned again, which is fine (an image with no container is out of scope).
error_path_audit.container_removed_mid_extraction: A get_archive 404 AFTER we hold the container surfaces as a not_found error inside a real payload (see the scenario), marked done on a 200 so it is not retried forever.
error_path_audit.server_refusal_is_200: The server answers 200 for every definitive outcome INCLUDING refusals (unsupported_distro, unscannable) so the agent marks the digest done and stops re-extracting the immutable image. Non-200 is transient only and releases the digest for retry.
error_path_audit.once_per_image_forever: The ImageInventoryCoordinator persists done digests to disk (image_inventory_done), so a Restart=always agent does not re-extract the whole host on restart; digests are immutable, so once done, done.

os_release_symlink.description: THE GOTCHA: /etc/os-release is a symlink to /usr/lib/os-release. The archive GET does NOT follow it -- it returns a tar with a SYMLINK entry plus stat['linkTarget'] = the ABSOLUTE target. The agent must re-request that target (NOT the tar entry's relative linkname) to read the file. An agent that skips this reports every Debian image as os-release-less / unscannable.

distroless_no_package_db.description: Distroless: /etc/os-release present (distro known) but no single-file /var/lib/dpkg/status (distroless keeps per-package status.d/ files). The DB GET 404s -> unsupported. packages is EMPTY but errors is NON-empty, so the server renders 'not scannable', never a false '0 vulnerabilities'.

container_removed_mid_extraction.description: The container disappears and the first archive GET (os-release) 404s. distro cannot be determined (null). Recorded as os_release/not_found: a removed container and a scratch image are indistinguishable at the archive API, so we record the step honestly and let the server label it. Never an empty-and-clean payload.

file_over_cap.description: The package DB streams past the 5 MB per-file cap, aborted MID-stream (running buf.tell() check, not after). os-release resolved first (distro known) then the DB read fails -> unscannable with a file_over_cap error, empty packages.

rpm_unsupported.description: AlmaLinux (RPM) image. os-release resolves to almalinux:9.3, but RPM extraction is phase 1.5 (rpmdb.sqlite holds binary header blobs). Reported unsupported with the distro known -- never silently empty. No DB read is attempted.

daemon_api_error.description: The daemon returns a non-404 API error for the package DB (500, permission denied, driver failure). Distinguished from not_found: the image is not declared unscannable-because-distroless, it simply could not be read this time. Carries a real api_error example. Messages are deterministic by design -- the raw SDK exception text varies by daemon version and is logged at debug instead, so the server can key on the message safely.

The parser is tolerant: it skips the partial + garbage stanzas and keeps the two complete ones (sorted). errors is empty -- a partial stanza among valid ones is not itself a scan failure.
